mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 8.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 8.5% but S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment increases while federal funds rate is low, it indicates economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies indicate stress but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth during an expansion signals positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate a strong housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales and employment indicate a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies are strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales during expansion indicate positive consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales are strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
